explanation: Titrating a strong acid with a strong base, moles of base added (Cb*Vb) neutralize moles of acid (Ca*Va) one-to-one. Before equivalence the pH comes from leftover H+ in the total volume; after equivalence it comes from excess OH-. At the equivalence point all acid is neutralized and only water and a neutral salt remain, so pH = 7 (at 25 C). The curve is nearly flat then jumps sharply through pH 7 at Veq = Ca*Va/Cb; the slider moves the volume of base added and the readout tracks pH.
bullets: Before Veq: pH set by excess H+ in total volume.
After Veq: pH set by excess OH-; sharp jump at Veq.
Equivalence of strong-strong is exactly pH 7 (violet dot).
